question: What do bees collect from flowers?

passage: The honeybee works hard every single day. It flies from flower to flower collecting nectar, which it stores in its honey stomach. Back at the hive, the bee passes the nectar to worker bees, who chew it and spread it through the hive. The water slowly evaporates, leaving behind the thick, sweet substance we call honey. A single colony of bees can visit millions of flowers and produce hundreds of kilograms of honey in one year.
